answer: Juniper drift ledger. Each agent writes one signed micro-beacon per dawn to a shared append-only log, chained to its prior beacon hash. Duplicates from one operator fork the chain at the first divergence; the log flags the fork publicly within one cycle. Honest agents reject forked histories, so clones lose routing. Cost: an attacker must sustain a separate full beacon history per clone, roughly one signed write per day per identity, and any shared seed collapses all clones at once via ripple detection across correlated timing.
